as_written_in_papers.quote: a pathogenic frameshift variant (c.103_104delGA;p.Asp35Phefs*20) in the LAMP-2 gene (NM_002294.3) predicted to cause truncation of the protein was detected in a heterozygous state, consistent with DD
LAMP-2 (NM_002294.3): c.103_104delGA;p.Asp35Phefs*20 in a hemizygous state

cases.statement: A Sardinian mother (Case 1, heterozygous) and her son (Case 2, hemizygous), both affected. The paper links them to a larger extended pedigree reported earlier.

people.label: Case 1
people.key_phenotypes: ventricular pre-excitation; atrial fibrillation; progressive LV dilatation and dysfunction (LVEF 22–25%) with mild LVH; ventricular fibrillation; heart transplantation at 49 with PAS-positive vacuoles in the explanted heart; TIA

quotes.quote: A routine ECG performed during pregnancy at 30 years of age revealed a ventricular pre-excitation pattern.
In the following years, palpitations recurred due to atrial fibrillation (AF), requiring two more transcatheter (TC) ablation treatments.
Further echocardiographic examinations during follow-up showed a progressive LV dilatation and dysfunction up to LVEF 25% with mild LV hypertrophy (Figure 1A and B).
After two subsequent episodes of ventricular fibrillation (VF) interrupted by the device, she was referred to our Heart Failure Unit (HFU) at the age of 48 years.
Cardiomyocytes were hypertrophic with prominent sarcoplasmic vacuoles filled with Periodic Acid–Schiff (PAS)-positive granules.

people.label: Case 2
people.key_phenotypes: third-degree AV block at 26; HCM pattern progressing to LVEF 25%; atrial fibrillation; mild cognitive impairment; chorioretinitis and high myopia; asymptomatic myopathy with CK 1254

quotes.quote: On admission, his ECG showed third-degree AVB.
Echocardiography revealed a HCM pattern with preserved EF (60%) and severe diastolic impairment.
we found a hypertrophic LV with severe systolic and diastolic dysfunction (LVEF 25%, E/A > 2, E/e′ 20)
| **Neurologic** | TIA | Mild cognitive impairment |
| **Ocular** | No | Chorioretinitis and high-grade myopia |
| Creatine phosphokinase (UI/L) | 73 | 1254 |

phenotype_specificity.statement: Case 1: coronary angiography excluded significant coronary disease, and the explanted heart showed PAS-positive vacuoles. Before genetic testing she was listed with a non-specific diagnosis. Case 2 shows cardiac and extracardiac features. The scope of genetic testing (single gene or panel) is not reported.

quotes.quote: A coronary angiogram excluded significant coronary artery disease, and a biventricular defibrillator [cardiac resynchronization therapy-defibrillator (CRT-D)] was implanted for primary prevention.
For this reason, at 48 years of age, she was listed for HT with a non-specific diagnosis of hypokinetic cardiomyopathy.
Cardiomyocytes were hypertrophic with prominent sarcoplasmic vacuoles filled with Periodic Acid–Schiff (PAS)-positive granules.

segregation.statement: The affected son inherited the variant from his affected heterozygous mother. The family history includes four sudden cardiac deaths, with genotypes not stated. Cascade screening of first-degree relatives was initially refused. The authors connect the family to an extended pedigree that includes two earlier Sardinian reports (pedigree figure only). No tested non-carriers are reported.

quotes.quote: Genetic testing revealed that he inherited the pathogenic variant from his mother.
The proband (Case 1) is a Caucasian female from Sardinia (Italy) with a familiar history of four SCD.
A cascade clinical and genetic screening was proposed to her first-degree family members but initially refused.

Investigation of our patients’ familial background revealed an extended pedigree, which included both the families described by Echaniz-Laguna et al.^13 and Muntoni et al.^14, encompassing what is, to the best of our knowledge, the largest family affected by DD published to date (Figure 3).

de_novo.statement: Not de novo in Case 2, who inherited the variant from his mother. Testing of Case 1's parents is not reported.

quotes.quote: Genetic testing revealed that he inherited the pathogenic variant from his mother.

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Two-base deletion causing a frameshift, p.(Asp35PhefsTer20). This agrees with the paper's p.Asp35Phefs*20, which the paper says is predicted to truncate the protein. The paper attributes Danon disease to primary LAMP-2 deficiency.

quotes.quote: predicted to cause truncation of the protein
DD has recently been shown to be due to primary deficiency of LAMP-2 leading to impaired autophagosome/lysosome function

authors_classification.statement: The authors call it a pathogenic frameshift variant and say it was reported before in a Sardinian family. No ACMG criteria are given.

quotes.quote: a pathogenic frameshift variant (c.103_104delGA;p.Asp35Phefs*20) in the LAMP-2 gene (NM_002294.3)
Our patients’ pathogenic variant was previously reported in France by Echaniz-Laguna et al.^13 in a Sardinian family with a history of cardiomyopathy.

concerns: The variant was reported before in the same extended family: Echaniz-Laguna et al. 2006 (PMID 16372318), plus the earlier Muntoni et al. 1994 family (PMID 7919971). Neither is in this batch, so they may hold more carriers or overlapping individuals. The panel may want them when weighing segregation.

The paper contradicts itself on Case 2's device: the timeline says complete AV block 'requiring a pacemaker' and the discussion says 'requiring pacemaker implantation', but the case text says 'an implantable cardioverter defibrillator (ICD) was implanted'.

Diagnosis timing is inconsistent: the abstract says Danon disease was diagnosed '1 year after' transplantation (timeline age 50), while the case text says genetic testing 'was proposed a few years later'.
The protein change stated in the paper agrees with the batch prediction, and the transcript NM_002294.3 is stated.
The method and scope of genetic testing are not described.
notes_for_panel: Mother-son pair with transcript-level HGVS stated. The extended Sardinian pedigree (earlier reports) lies outside this batch and could add segregation data.
